rationale: MercariSearchUrlService.BuildSearch previously only added itemStatuses for the sold direction (itemStatuses=2), leaving the active direction ('sold: false') completely unfiltered and returning every item status Mercari tracks (on_sale, trading, sold_out) under one inflated count. A live comparison against the real Mercari search endpoint (via the AIOWebScraper Functions API, run from the sanctioned S:\scraper checkout with domain filtering disabled and the off-screen browser patch applied) confirmed itemStatuses=1 is the on-sale-only filter: for 'ps5 controller', the unfiltered active search reported count=17958 with a page-1 status mix of {on_sale: 94, trading: 6}, itemStatuses=1 reported count=8095 with 100/100 items on_sale (and the server echoed back criteria.itemStatuses=[1], confirming Mercari itself interprets it that way), and itemStatuses=2 (the pre-existing sold filter) reported count=9864 with a page-1 mix of {trading: 98, sold_out: 2} -- 8095 + 9864 = 17959, matching the unfiltered count almost exactly (off by 1 from live count drift between the two fetches a few minutes apart), proving itemStatuses={1,2} partitions the unfiltered result set. The same comparison repeated against a narrow price band (minPrice=20.01, maxPrice=50, the shape MercariPriceBandCollector actually issues) reproduced the same pattern (banded itemStatuses=1: count=1664, 100/100 on_sale; banded unfiltered: count=4421, {on_sale: 94, trading: 6}), confirming the filter behaves consistently at both the whole-catalogue and single-band scope the collector uses. MercariSearchUrlService.BuildSearch now sends AddIfPresent(query, "itemStatuses", request.Sold ? "2" : "1") unconditionally, so every active-direction search (both BuildSearch(searchTerm, sold, page) and the banded IPriceBandSearchUrlService.BuildSearch used by MercariPriceBandCollector) is now restricted to on-sale items, while the sold direction's itemStatuses=2 is untouched. A new fixture tests/MarketMakerEtl.Tests.Unit/Fixtures/Mercari/search-payload-active-filtered.json pins a trimmed capture of the real itemStatuses=1 response (count=8095, criteria.itemStatuses=[1], two real on_sale items) and MercariSearchPayloadParsesToListingsTests asserts every parsed listing is IsSold=false and the reported TotalCount matches the captured 8095, so a regression that stops sending or silently drops the filter would be caught by a real-data-shaped test rather than only a synthetic one. No production parsing code changed: MercariSearchParser/MercariSearchPayloadParser already read the same 'status' field for every response regardless of which itemStatuses value was requested, and the live evidence confirms the filtered JSON-payload response has the identical shape (data.search.count/itemsList) as the unfiltered one, so the existing parser handles it without modification -- all nine live captures in this session (across both the full-catalogue and price-banded active/sold/unfiltered searches) came back as JSON payloads rather than rendered HTML cards, so the AIOWebScraper#150 HTML-card code path could not be directly exercised in this session; that path reads the same data-itemstatus attribute used by the existing sold/trading/sold_out tests and is unaffected by which itemStatuses value produced the page, but a real run through the full ETL stack (scope item 3, tracked as AC-3) is the only way to observe it end to end. MercariPriceBandCollector, PriceBandQueue and the #59 sold-direction override (MergeAndCountNew forcing IsSold=true for the sold direction, which still wins on merge over an active-direction copy of the same listing id) are untouched: all of MercariPriceBandCollectorTests' existing stubbed-URL-service scenarios construct SearchPageResult data directly and never depend on which itemStatuses string the real MercariSearchUrlService would have produced, so they continue to pass unmodified and prove the override and merge/pruning logic still work exactly as #59 left them.
declaredRedTestsNote: MercariSearchUrlServiceTests.Should_target_the_mercari_search_page_with_the_search_term (pre-existing, asserted Does.Not.Contain("itemStatuses=2") for the active direction) was left unchanged, since that assertion is still true after this change -- itemStatuses=1 is what active now sends, not itemStatuses=2 -- and a new dedicated test was added alongside it rather than rewriting the old one's intent.
